It has no handling for missing settings.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Loads settings and prints key prefixes
sections.what: Loads the environment settings from the parent folder and prints the database address along with the first 25 characters of the public and service keys.
sections.why: Likely reason: to check the settings were loaded, though showing part of the service key goes further than needed.
sections.watch_out: The service role key prefix is printed in full view, so it could be exposed in logs or screen shares.

summary: Loads the Next.js environment settings and prints the database address and the start of two secret keys.
purpose: Helps confirm the settings are being read correctly.
why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: to debug why the database connection fails.
how: Load the environment settings from the parent folder. Print the database address. Print the first 25 characters of the public key and of the service key, with dots after them.
inputs: The environment settings in the project folder.
outputs: Three printed lines to the terminal.
risks: The service role key is partly printed to the terminal and to any logs that capture it. That key can have full database access.
debug: If values print as undefined, the environment file is missing or in another folder. Confirm the file location and the variable names.
